key_insight: REFLEX uses a fast typed decision layer (Jev) to route only low-confidence or generative cases to a strong LLM, preserving success while cutting expensive model calls.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical control strategy for LLM agents: keep routine bounded decisions cheap, and reserve high-cost reasoning for uncertain or open-ended steps.
method: Jev handles selective, typed action decisions
A strong LLM is called only when confidence is low or generation is needed
The design is tested across multiple fallback families
evidence_signal: On a frozen 100-task benchmark, REFLEX achieved 95% success while reducing strong-model calls by 72.7%; additional BFCL and τ-style evaluations compared its gains against a cheap generative cascade.
watch_item: Benefits may be limited when ordinary routing is already highly accurate, so added complexity may not pay off in all deployment settings.
paper_title: REFLEX with Jev for Efficient Selective Control in LLM Agents
